title: Manhattan Bridge Digital Twin
summary: A source-governed, part-addressable digital twin of the Manhattan Bridge for browser rendering and HO-scale study, in which every dimension traces to a registered source with a confidence grade.

narrative.problem: No existing 3D model of the Manhattan Bridge is authoritative, and there is no public measured drawing of it — the HAER survey contains photographs and no drawings — so a detailed model easily ends up inventing dimensions it cannot source.
narrative.decision: Official dimensions and archival drawings in GEOMETRY-CONTROL.md are the control geometry: scripts parse it and carry no numbers of their own, anything without a registered source is tagged confidence D, and geometry provenance is drawn as solid, dashed and dotted outlines so uncertainty is visible by default.
narrative.tradeoff: Refusing to invent dimensions keeps the model honest, but 66 of 103 parts remain grade D and 14 of 78 control values are placeholders; photographs can grade materials but cannot promote a dimension above D without scale control.
narrative.limitation: The remaining placeholders wait on NYC DOT and MTA record drawings that are not public, for which a FOIL request is prepared; none of the 253 audit photographs has been reviewed yet, and CI skips schema validation of the published contract documents.
narrative.caveat: Most parts are inferred or placeholder geometry. Switching off inferred and assumed parts in the viewer leaves the towers, anchorages and station markers — the whole of what the model can be said to document.

images.alt: Black-and-white HAER photograph NY-127-7 looking up at a Manhattan Bridge main tower, its lattice-braced steel legs rising from a masonry pier, with main cables, suspenders and the stiffening truss deck receding across the river.
images.caption: A registered source photograph of a main tower. Photographs enter the model only with a source ID, licence, attribution and checksum, and can grade materials but not dimensions.

images.alt: Photo review page titled 'Manhattan Bridge — material and arrangement evidence — photo review' with Save decisions and filter controls, a counter reading 0 kept, 0 skipped, 253 undecided, and definitions for categories such as masonry, arch, truss, steel surface and cable.
images.caption: The photograph audit sheet: each category states what a photo can establish and which open question it feeds; all 253 photographs are still undecided.
images.credit: Screenshot of the Manhattan Bridge Digital Twin site

images.caption: Crowdsourced views come from where people stand, which covers the underside well but cannot see inside the truss bays where placeholders remain.
